# ABAC-002: Fail closed on evaluation errors
Severity: blocker. Enforced by review today.

## Rule
Applies to code that asks for an access decision: calls to
AccessEvaluation, the lookups that build its subject (the user, the
channel role, BuildAccessControlSubject), and the PDP itself.

Any error, timeout or missing input on the way to a decision ends in
deny. Return false, return the error to a caller that denies, or leave
the item out of a list. Never return true, and never carry on as if the
check passed.

These are not errors, so they keep their documented defaults: ABAC is
turned off, there is no requesting user, or no policy applies
(AccessDecision.IsNoPolicy).

## Why
If an error ends in allow, an engine outage or one bad attribute turns
into open access for everyone.

## Bad
decision, err := acs.AccessEvaluation(rctx, req)
if err != nil {
    rctx.Logger().Warn("evaluation failed", mlog.Err(err))
    return true // the engine is down, let the request through
}

## Good
decision, err := acs.AccessEvaluation(rctx, req)
if err != nil {
    rctx.Logger().Warn("evaluation failed, denying", mlog.Err(err))
    return false
}
return decision.Decision

## How reviewers check
Follow every error branch between building the subject and using the
decision, to its return. Cite the file and line of any branch that
returns true, or a result its caller reads as allow, or that carries on
as if the check passed.

## Exceptions
- Plugin evaluation may answer an engine error with a no-policy result,
  but only after confirming that no policy governs the resource.
- Render hints in access_control_decision.go only decide which buttons
  to show. An action registered without FailClosedOnError may fall back
  to its default, because enforcement checks again live.
